SUMMARY: Purchasing role responsible for operational buying and monthly monitoring of expiring supplier compliance certificates.
INFOBOX:
Role code: role-pur-senior-buyer
Module: Purchasing
Primary duty: Supplier certificate expiry monitoring
Review cycle: Monthly (first working day)
Lookahead window: 90 days
Governing policy: AMD-SUP-2026-02
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
The Senior Buyer is an operational role within the Northbridge Cycles purchasing department responsible for key procurement tasks and supplier compliance monitoring.[^r1] Under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], the role is assigned routine oversight of battery certification compliance across active vendors.[^r1] As of 26 October 2026, the Senior Buyer ensures timely renewals by tracking certificate expirations well before shipments occur.[^r1]

## Responsibilities

The senior buyer is required to run the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day of every month using a 90-day window.[^r1] Following the generation of this report, the senior buyer must contact all suppliers identified with expiring [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]].[^r1]

## See also

* [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy]]
* [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy]]
* [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 Certificates]]

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (superseded):** From 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3].
* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## See also

* [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy]]
* [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001 Purchase Policy]]
* [[role-pur-senior-buyer|Senior Buyer]]

SUMMARY: AMD-SUP-2026-02 tightens UN 38.3 battery certificate validity to 12 months issue age and 60 days validity post-order from 1 September 2026.
INFOBOX:
Document Code: AMD-SUP-2026-02
Version: 1.0
Author: L. Moreno
Owner: Purchase department
Effective Date: 2026-09-01
Status: CURRENT
CONFLICTS:
- superseded | UN 38.3 certificates are accepted only if issued within the last 12 months with a valid-to date at least 60 days after order placement date for orders placed from 1 September 2026 | Certificates issued within 24 months and not expired were accepted under the old rule; counts as no certificate for new orders | r2,r3
BODY:
AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] effective 1 September 2026 that tightens the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1][^r2]. Under this amendment, certificates must have been issued within the last 12 months and remain valid for at least 60 days following order placement[^r2]. It governs all new purchase orders placed for lithium-cell parts as of today, 26 October 2026[^r2][^r3].

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document Code | AMD-SUP-2026-02 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Author | L. Moreno |
| Owner | Purchase department |
| Effective Date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | CURRENT |

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
Effective 1 September 2026, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4.4 is replaced such that a [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2]. A certificate meeting the old rule of being issued within 24 months and not expired counts as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, whereas orders released before that date are not affected[^r3].

### 2. Why
The policy change was prompted by a July 2026 incident where a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed Northbridge's incoming abuse test because the cell maker had changed[^r4].

### 3. What purchase staff must do
Purchase staff must check the issue date and valid-to date of a lithium-cell part's certificate against the new rule before raising an order[^r5]. The [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] must run the certificate-expiry report per MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 on the first working day of each month with a 90-day window and notify every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate expires within it[^r6]. All other parts of POL-SUP-003 §4 remain in effect[^r7].

## Versions and conflicts
- **Today's rule (effective 2026-09-01)**: For new orders placed from 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2][^r3].
- **Older rule (superseded)**: Certificates issued within 24 months and not expired were accepted under POL-SUP-003 §4.4; these now count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date are not affected[^r3].
- **Kind**: `superseded`[^r2][^r3].

## See also
* [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy]]
* [[role-pur-senior-buyer|Senior Buyer]]
* [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|topic-un-38-3-certificates]]

POL-SUP-003 sets out Northbridge Cycles' mandatory standards and qualification rules for all suppliers. As of 1 September 2026, the policy incorporates updated compliance requirements for lithium battery documentation under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]]. In force today, battery purchases governed by this policy require valid [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] meeting strict issue-date and forward-validity criteria.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| Code | POL-SUP-003 |
| Type | Policy |
| Effective date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | current |

## Clauses

### Clause 4.4

On 1 September 2026, Clause 4.4 of POL-SUP-003 was replaced by [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]] to require [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] to have been issued within 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after order placement[^r1].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (effective 2026-09-01):** Clause 4.4 requires [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] to have been issued within 12 months and to be valid for at least 60 days after order placement ([^r1]).
* **Older rule:** The original wording of Clause 4.4 prior to 1 September 2026 was replaced ([^r1]).
* **Kind:** `superseded`.

* [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy]]
